messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@northridgebank.com>, Tom Berger <tberger@northridgebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-14T15:12:00Z
Subject: Security acceptance kickoff & evidence todo

Hi Alicia / Tom — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our demo + compliance discussion and explicit next steps so we’re all aligned.

High-level takeaway
- Primary goal: Put Redwood into an evaluation track for production inference across their US region with SOC 2 Type II and audit-log retention to meet NRBank policy.
- Main risks you flagged: audit log retention (7 years for some flows), pen-test evidence for hosted endpoints, and DPA clauses around data residency and subprocessor list.

What we committed to by next Wednesday (2025-08-20):
1) Provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II summary + mapping to NRBank controls (attached: Redwood_SOC2_Type_II_summary.pdf)
2) Share our audit-log retention matrix showing event types, retention windows, and extraction endpoints (attached: audit_log_retention_matrix.xlsx)
3) Deliver the latest redacted penetration test report and a one-page explanation of scope (attached: redwood-pen-test-redacted.pdf)
4) Draft DPA talking points and a suggested narrow exception for retention windows for archived logs — we’ll surface exact language via the DocuSign preview link.

Immediate asks for you: please confirm
- Which specific audit events (by name) must be retained for 7 years vs. 1 year? If you can send the list or a short spreadsheet we’ll map it directly.
- Who is the technical reviewer on your side for log extraction tests?

Operational notes / mitigation strategy we discussed
- For long-tail retention we propose a tiered approach: short-term hot logs on SSD for 90–180 days and an encrypted archive bucket with retention lifecycle for compliant long-term storage.
- For pen-test evidence we will provide redacted findings + remediation status; full reports can be made available under an NDA if required.

Attachments referenced below. I’ll follow up with a HubSpot record that contains the MAP and timeline. If it’s helpful, we can schedule a 30-min call next week to go through the matrix line-by-line.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni

Subject: Re: Security acceptance kickoff & evidence todo

Vivek — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Event types we need for 7yr retention: E-Transaction-Auth, Settlement-Record, Audit-Access-Log. I’ll attach the formal list in a follow-up by EOD.
2) Technical reviewer: Tom Berger (cc’d) will validate extraction endpoints. He prefers a test window next week (Aug 21–22).
3) SOC 2: the summary is fine for initial screening, but our InfoSec will require the full report under an NDA before production access.

Requests:
- Please provide an export sample (sanitized) of the audit_log_retention_matrix showing one example of E-Transaction-Auth retention and the extraction path.
- Can you confirm whether hosted inference logs include raw prompt content or only metadata by default? We need to flag any prompt retention for PII.

Tom / Vivek — I’m happy to run the extraction test with you next week. If we can get the audit sample and the SOC redaction rules today, that will speed our procurement review.

Thanks, Alicia
Alicia Ramos
VP, InfoSec Operations
North Ridge Bank

Thanks Alicia — quick answers and next artifacts attached.

Audit sample: attached sheet (audit_log_retention_matrix.xlsx) includes the E-Transaction-Auth row with extraction path and an example CSV export column list.
Prompt retention: default hosted telemetry only stores metadata (request_id, model_version, token_counts, timestamp, response_hash). Raw prompt content is not persisted unless a customer enables "developer logs" for debugging; for enterprise customers we default that off and can enforce via config.

SOC 2 / pen-test: the attached SOC2 summary explains what is available in the full report (which we can share under NDA). The redacted pen-test includes scope boundaries and remediations to date.

Proposed MAP (mutual action plan) highlights
- Aug 18: NRBank to confirm final list of audit events for 7yr retention (Alicia)
- Aug 21–22: extraction test window with Tom (technical verification)
- Aug 25: provide full SOC2 to NRBank under NDA (Redwood legal to initiate)
- Aug 29: procurement + DPA review comments due (NRBank legal)

Doc links / quick actions
- Drive folder for artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cRedwoodEvidence
- HubSpot opportunity: HS-98234 (I added MAP checklist)
- DPA preview: https://www.redwoodinference.com/dpa/preview/NDG-1457

I’ve attached the three artifacts referenced previously. If Tom is available for a 30-min slot on Aug 21 at 10:00 PT I’ll put an invite.

—Vivek

Folks — forwarding the thread after Alicia confirmed the event names and the ask for a sanitized export sample. Action items for internal owners: 

- Marissa: please own the extraction test logistics with Tom (Aug 21–22). We need a sanitized CSV sample ready by EOD Aug 20 and an IAM token that will be valid only for the test window.
- Soojin: legal follow-up — start the NDA + DocuSign request so we can deliver the full SOC2 on Aug 25. Also prepare a one-paragraph redaction policy to attach.

Notes & constraints:
- The long-term retention lifecycle will be an encrypted archive; compute access is restricted. We should confirm export performance SLAs (Tom may test for large-volume exports).
- If procurement requests a change to retention windows in the DPA, flag it to me before committing.

I’ll coordinate the calendar invites and upload the sanitized sample to the Drive folder once ready.

Thanks — Vivek
